about: Engines (DESIGN 5.11): processing modules compiled once to WebAssembly that every stack hosts alike. An engine is a plain WebAssembly module that exports its `memory`, `clarity_alloc(len) -> place` and `clarity_free(place, len)`, and each of its functions under its own name as `(place, len) -> i64`. To call one, the host writes the arguments as a JSON array (UTF-8) into room from clarity_alloc and calls the function with its place and length; the engine takes that room over. The function gives the place and length of its answer packed in an i64 (place in the high 32 bits), `{"value": ...}` or `{"error": "why"}`, which the host reads and gives back with clarity_free. Values are JSON as everywhere in Clarity: integers as numbers, decimals and money as exact text, enums by name, records as objects of their fields. An engine imports nothing, and a host refuses a module that imports anything, that is no WebAssembly, or that lacks the interface or a declared function, when it loads it. `engine` is test.wasm, built from engines/test.
